source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED treats the command as vendor-defined security protocol. Official IPMI v2.0 section 22.16 instead defines App command 39h, exact unauthenticated framing, request fields, positive response and named error completion codes.

old_problem: Both source procedure and criteria are TBD, so historical reviews left the case Pending/BLOCKED and required a vendor-defined challenge protocol, crypto, replay, expiry and cleanup. Direct standards research shows the named command itself is not OEM: IPMI v2.0 fully defines the legacy session-challenge request and response. The remaining decisions are applicability, target channel/auth type and a dedicated test identity, not unknown core semantics.
disposition_reason: Replace the TBD only in the Review layer with the standard Get Session Challenge conformance flow. First prove the selected channel advertises the requested IPMI 1.5 authentication type and that the Project security profile permits this optional legacy function. Send exactly one unauthenticated App/39h request using a dedicated ephemeral enabled username, validate the 00h response shape—four-byte little-endian temporary Session ID plus sixteen-byte challenge—and never send Activate Session. Validate the specified invalid-user and disabled-null-user completion paths only when included in the approved matrix. Redact challenge/session values, preserve security logs, prove active-session count is unchanged and let temporary state expire. If the platform intentionally omits legacy IPMI 1.5 challenge support, authoritative platform/security SPEC plus capability evidence yields N/A; it is not Pending.
decision_basis: XLSX rows 1015 and physical adjacent 1016, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. Wistron-BMC-00305-V002 is unique. Formal queue sequence 58 is row 1016 / variant 5b99910116ad61a7.
IPMI v2.0 section 22.16 / Table 22-21 defines Get Session Challenge as App NetFn 06h command 39h sent unauthenticated: session authentication NONE, sequence and Session ID all zero, no AuthCode.

The request is exactly byte 1 authentication type with high nibble reserved and low nibble 0h None, 1h MD2, 2h MD5, 4h straight password/key or 5h OEM; bytes 2-17 are a sixteen-byte username, all zero only for null User 1.

A success response has completion 00h, a four-byte temporary Session ID least-significant byte first and sixteen bytes of challenge data. Completion 81h means invalid username and 82h means null username/User 1 is not enabled.

The specification explicitly says the returned temporary Session ID is not an active session until Activate Session. Therefore this row does not need to authenticate, send a password, prove payload crypto or close an active session; doing so would add unrelated risk and overlap later session cases.

Get Channel Authentication Capabilities precedes this optional legacy path and determines supported authentication types. A Project that disables IPMI 1.5/RMCP legacy sessions for security may mark this case N/A only with versioned target policy and capability evidence.

ED-03 and ED-13 permit a standards-based BMC contract while forbidding guessed OEM auth types; ED-15 requires evidence for N/A; ED-18/ED-30 forbid invented security thresholds; ED-19 preserves audit logs; ED-28's exact-tool/isolation/recovery principle applies; ED-33 through ED-38 distinguish finite readiness inputs from core unknowns and prohibit automatic retry or false hardware verdicts.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Get Session Challenge (App 06h/39h) legacy conformance
test_case.purpose: Verify the target's explicitly supported legacy IPMI session-challenge command returns the standard temporary-session/challenge framing for one dedicated enabled user, enforces approved invalid/null-user errors, creates no active authenticated session, preserves audit evidence and exposes no reusable authentication material.
required_package: Target BMC identity, firmware and channel map plus protected management network; versioned Project security policy stating whether IPMI 1.5 Get Session Challenge is required, permitted or intentionally unsupported
Preflight Get Channel Authentication Capabilities evidence for the exact channel and requested standard authentication type; OEM type 5h needs separate vendor authority and is not guessed

Dedicated ephemeral least-privilege test username encoded to exactly sixteen bytes with Project-approved padding, enabled on the selected channel; null User 1 state is documented if the 82h subcase is used

Validated sessionless IPMI 1.5 conformance harness able to emit App NetFn 06h command 39h with auth NONE, zero sequence/Session ID and no AuthCode, parse byte-accurate response, redact raw challenge/temp ID and avoid shell/process secret exposure

Bounded test matrix: one positive request, one intentionally invalid nonproduction username for 81h, and optional all-zero null-user request for 82h only when User 1 is disabled and security owner approves

Pre/post Get Session Info or equivalent active-session evidence, security/audit-log retention, temporary-challenge expiry/invalidation observation, rate-limit/lockout abort and security-owner point confirmation
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SECURITY-CONFORMANCE PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve audit/session baseline; do not clear logs. Confirm the exact channel advertises the selected standard auth type and obtain immediate approval for the dedicated account. With a validated sessionless harness, encode an IPMI v1.5 request header with authentication NONE, sequence 00000000h, Session ID 00000000h and no AuthCode; send App NetFn 06h / command 39h with request byte 1 `${AUTH_TYPE & 0x0F}` and bytes 2-17 `${TEST_USERNAME}` exactly sixteen bytes, zero padded per the approved encoding. Send once. In volatile parser memory verify completion 00h and exactly twenty response-data bytes after completion: temporary Session ID bytes 2-5 little-endian and challenge bytes 6-21; emit only length, structural checks, non-secret correlation token/digest and redacted values. Do not send Activate Session. If approved, send one request with a guaranteed-nonexistent dedicated name and require 81h; send the all-zero username only when the null user is documented disabled and require 82h. Verify no active session was added, preserve audit/rate-limit evidence and wait the approved temporary-state expiry/invalidation interval. Never use production usernames/secrets, request unsupported/OEM auth, log raw challenge or temp ID, brute-force, replay, activate, clear logs or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: Preflight capability and Project policy agree that the selected legacy auth type is applicable. The single positive unauthenticated 06h/39h request returns completion 00h, a structurally valid four-byte little-endian temporary Session ID and exactly sixteen challenge bytes, with no active session because Activate Session was never sent. Approved invalid username returns 81h; the optional disabled-null-user subcase returns 82h. No raw challenge/session value or secret is persisted, no lockout/rate-limit/authentication degradation occurs, active-session count is unchanged, temporary state expires/invalidates per policy and security audit health remains intact. If legacy support is intentionally absent, authoritative policy/capability evidence produces N/A rather than execution or PASS.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target/channel/auth applicability, byte-accurate sessionless framing, one 00h response with 4+16 data layout, approved 81h and conditional 82h results when in scope, challenge/session redaction, no Activate Session, unchanged active-session inventory, clean expiry/audit state and no security degradation. A transport reply alone, authenticated wrapper as sole evidence, wrong length/endianness, reserved auth type, OEM type without vendor definition, production identity, raw challenge capture, unexpected active session, lockout/rate-limit event, retry or missing cleanup cannot pass. Missing target/account/harness inputs are NOT READY; documented unsupported legacy function is N/A, not a fabricated success.
safety_gate: Use an isolated management network and dedicated ephemeral least-privilege identity. Display target/channel/auth type, exact subcases, redaction and abort conditions for security-owner confirmation before sending anything.

Do not clear audit/SEL/security logs. Preserve baseline and final active-session/authentication health; never log raw challenge, temporary Session ID, credentials or packet payload containing reusable material.

The harness must send the standard unauthenticated NULL session header and exactly one request per planned subcase. No Activate Session, password proof, auth downgrade, OEM type guess, replay, fuzzing or brute force is authorized.

Stop on unexpected completion/length, repeated/predictable material observed by the in-memory checker, active-session allocation, rate limit, lockout, audit loss or management instability; revoke/disable only the dedicated identity through the approved owner path.
No automatic retry. A timeout or malformed/ambiguous response is retained as first evidence and escalated without another challenge request.
Delete volatile raw buffers after structural validation, retain only approved redacted metadata/digests and confirm temporary state expiration plus normal BMC access.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant, BMC/firmware/channel, Project legacy-auth applicability policy and Get Channel Authentication Capabilities decode
Security approval, dedicated account metadata without secret, exact 16-byte encoding rule, harness/version/hash and nonproduction invalid/null-user matrix
Redacted request header fields proving auth NONE/zero sequence/zero Session ID/no AuthCode and App 06h/39h request length/type/username-length checks
Redacted positive completion, exact response length, temporary-ID endianness check, sixteen-byte challenge-presence check and one-way evidence token without raw values
Approved 81h and conditional 82h completion evidence, with no repeated guesses or lockout/rate-limit event
Pre/post active-session inventory, temporary-state expiry/invalidation, preserved audit/security health, dedicated-identity disposal and engineer verdict/N/A authority
test_case.recovery: No active session should exist because Activate Session is prohibited. On unexpected state, timeout, exposure or lockout, stop without retry, zero volatile buffers, preserve redacted audit evidence and notify the security/BMC owner. Terminate only a positively identified test session through the supported owner procedure if one was unexpectedly activated; do not close unrelated sessions. Revoke/rotate/disable only the dedicated test identity as approved, wait for temporary challenge state to expire or use the documented vendor invalidation path, then verify active-session inventory, audit integrity and management access before closure.

source_conflict.reason: The TBD fields are completed from the exact standard named by the Items. Generic log clearing is removed from the executable Review layer because audit preservation is mandatory; Master remains unchanged.

blocked.reason: IPMI v2.0 supplies the complete protocol schema and Expected Result. Channel/auth applicability, dedicated username and secure harness are finite Project execution inputs, so the case is NOT READY until bound but no core protocol decision remains.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Section 22.16/Table 22-21 defines unauthenticated Get Session Challenge App 39h framing, auth type and 16-byte username request, 81h/82h errors, little-endian temporary Session ID and 16-byte challenge; section 22.17 states the session is not active until Activate Session.

project_authority: The Project security/BMC owners decide whether the optional legacy IPMI 1.5 challenge path is applicable, approve the exact standard auth type, isolated account, subcases, harness/redaction and temporary-state policy. They issue PASS/FAIL/N/A; approval cannot permit production credentials, OEM guesses, raw challenge retention, activation/replay, log clearing, retries or claim support when the capability/policy says legacy auth is disabled.
